guard: a declared completion marker downgrades a KILLED to INCONCLUSIVE, and only for a suite that declared one
why: This file used to grade a failure-vocabulary constant that no longer exists. `main` replaced that whole approach with a baseline-transcript comparison, which answers the same question without a grader guessing a suite's output conventions, so the constant and its six mutations went with it. What remains is the one behaviour that survived the merge on its own merits, and it is graded by exactly the two cells that pin it.

mutations.name: the completion check is disabled outright
mutations.expectRed: a suite that declared a completion marker gets INCONCLUSIVE, not KILLED, when the run stops early
mutations.cell: a suite that declared a completion marker gets INCONCLUSIVE, not KILLED, when the run stops early

mutations.name: THE OPT-IN: the check stops asking whether the suite asked for it
mutations.expectRed: ...and THE SAME RUN with no marker declared is still KILLED, so this is opt-in and not a new default
mutations.cell: ...and THE SAME RUN with no marker declared is still KILLED, so this is opt-in and not a new default
mutations.note: With no marker declared this reads `includes(undefined)`, which is false, so every unmarked suite starts grading INCONCLUSIVE. That is the exact regression the control cell exists to catch, and it is what `a real red followed by a crash is still KILLED` would silently lose. Aimed at the control rather than at the feature, because a feature cell going red proves the feature is wired and only the control proves it did not become global.
